title: Customer-specific eval hiccups caused by seed-order + stop-token resolution mismatch across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-priority customer escalations reported inconsistent eval outputs for a small set of customers after the sampling-defaults & stop-token normalization rollout. Failures manifest as either truncated JSON payloads or runaway generations depending on deployment mode (hosted vs private). Root cause appears tied to ordering differences in middleware that stamp RNG seed and the step that normalizes stop/termination tokens. This ticket tracks the hotfix, repro work, and the longer-term deterministic ordering guarantees.
steps_to_repro: 1) Use customer's canonical prompt set (attached reference prompts link).
2) Call hosted API with the customer's headers + sampling unspecified (relying on defaults). Observe stable generation with proper termination in ~95% of repeats.
3) Call same prompts via aDedicated pool configured with identical model variant; observe a subset produce truncated JSON or missing end tokens intermittently.
4) Run same prompts in Private deployment (VPC) where routing uses fallback model variant; observe differences from both hosted and dedicated behaviors.
5) Capture request/response traces for mismatches; correlate with middleware logs (seed assignment, sampling config, stop-token-normalizer) and KV cache hits.
technical_root_cause: A non-deterministic ordering bug in the request processing pipeline caused the RNG seed to be applied after stop-token normalization in some routing paths (notably private fallback and dedicated overlay). Because stop-token normalization can rewrite or canonicalize multi-byte/UTF8 markers, applying seed-based sampling after normalization changed tokenization boundaries and caused inconsistent early termination or absence of stop signals. Additionally, a race where the fallback route replaced model variant post-seed-stamp produced a seed-model mismatch leading to entropy shifts (different tokenization maps).
mitigation_steps: Hotfix deployed: reorder pipeline so stop-token normalization ALWAYS runs before seed stamping in the request path. Patch merged to routing and private-agent branches (PRs linked below).
Temporary change: pin fallback routing to same model-quantization family until deterministic ordering tests pass across environments.
Customer communication: rolling update and mitigation notes posted to the escalation thread; offered dedicated dry-run window for impacted customers.
long_term_fix: Introduce an explicit pipeline contract: canonicalization -> stop-token mapping -> sampling/seeding -> model routing -> execution. Add strong unit and e2e tests that simulate variant switch after seed application and assert parity. Also add a middleware invariant checker that fails CI if order changes. Plan to backfill telemetry that logs the canonical pipeline step IDs per request for future forensics.
testing_plan: Add deterministic replay harness that replays historical customer calls across hosted/dedicated/private and compares token-level outputs.
Add unit tests to ensure stop-token normalizer idempotency and that RNG seed is invariant to normalizer output.
Run 48-hour canary comparing production traffic vs testbed for parity metrics (BLEU/JSON-parse success/termination-token-latency).
Create synthetic fuzz suite that generates multi-byte stop token variants and asserts consistent termination across all routing layers.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix to runtime-1.22 branch and create canary image.
2) Deploy canary to 1% of Hosted traffic for 6 hours, monitor eval-parity dashboard and customer escalations channel.
3) If stable, expand to Dedicated control plane and a single Private customer test VPC.
4) Full rollout to Dedicated pools and Private agents after 24h stability window.
5) Post-rollout retrospective and mark release notes.
